body:
NARROW HOLD ADDRESSED. Revised candidate 6e57168 on m1/chart-eligibility, base e100b5a (current
main, rebased and re-gated on it). Supersedes f849104.

YOU WERE RIGHT AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: term production happens BEFORE eligibility is
consulted, so my "positive control" was a control on PROVIDER EXECUTION, not on eligibility. It
asserted the term was present and the totals differed, and both of those survive
`structuralEligible = false` untouched. I called it a control on the strength of what it was named
rather than what it could fail on.

Your literals are in and both mutations now die:
  structuralEligible = false     expected 0.9655172413793105 but was 1.0
  old provider+unit predicate    expected 0.9552238805970149 but was 0.8311688311688312
thirteen siblings passing in each. I pinned the absent tuple as well
(0.961038961038961, 1.3621621621621622); it does not kill either mutant, but it makes the pair a
stated comparison rather than two numbers that happen to differ.

I reproduced your charted tuple exactly on my tree before mutating, so we are measuring the same
candidate. And your predicted mutant value (1.0, 1.2) is exactly what came out - full support,
because once Structural leaves the eligible set nothing eligible went unmeasured. That is a clean
demonstration that the support figure is only as honest as the eligible set it is computed against.

WHAT I TAKE FROM THIS ONE. Both of my controls today were named for what I wanted them to prove
rather than derived from what would falsify them, and both times you found the gap by mutating the
thing itself instead of reading the test. The chart law I got right only because the number I had
happened to be the support figure; here the analogous assertion did not exist and I did not notice
the difference. The rule I am taking is narrower than "write positive controls": A CONTROL MUST NAME
THE MUTATION IT KILLS. If I cannot say which edit turns it red, I have not written a control, I have
written a description.

Gate: seven modules via reference-scope.sh, seven totals counted, zero failures - align 211,
codec 108, embedBench 64, embedGrakern 28, fixtures 117, interview 92, laws 86. scalafmtCheckAll
last, clean. Scratch probes untracked and emptied, excluded from the 211.

Holds unchanged: cost.scala rv-01M17N8HH49AH9NQTK2MV4CS0T, CostSuite.scala
rv-01M17M70JNTR5M0G2GXM6QTFKP. Nothing else.

SEPARATE, not part of this candidate and not asking you to act: I posted a measured finding on
bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9. A semantic provider that abstains entirely and one that measures
exactly 0.5 produce bit-identical cells - same term, same support 0.9552238805970149, same total
1.046875 - because dSem = clamp(semantic.orElse(unit, node, missingSemantic=0.5)) and Semantic lives
in `always`, so it is never recorded in missingTerms and always counted as measured. That cell
reports missingTerms = Set(Chart, Structural, Sensory), naming three absent terms and omitting the
substituted one. It is wired in production at embed-bench/report.scala:283 with the embed-core
channel whose docstring promises "Abstentions stay Missing" - the promise is kept to the boundary of
the cost model and defeated one line inside it. I have not opened a candidate; chief has a
sequencing question from me.
